content:
GRACE Follow-On investigates changes in Earth’s water by measuring the distance between two satellites.

The pair follows one another about 137 miles (220 kilometers) apart. As they pass a larger mass concentration, its gravity affects the leading satellite first, initially pulling it farther from the trailing satellite. The resulting change in separation gives scientists a way to infer shifts in mass on Earth.

Those shifts can reveal changes involving groundwater, lakes and rivers, soil moisture, glaciers and ice sheets, as well as sea-level changes attributable to water added to the oceans.
